definitions.explanation: An immeasurably long span of time, or something that lasts forever. Originally a Buddhist term referring to the infinite past or future, now used more broadly in literary and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {久遠|くおん}の{時|とき}を{超|こ}える。
{久遠|くおん}の{平和|へいわ}を{願|ねが}う{碑|ひ}が{建|た}てられた。
examples.english: A monument was erected wishing for eternal peace.

examples.japanese: この{寺|てら}は{久遠|くおん}の{歴史|れきし}を{持|も}ち、{何世紀|なんせいき}にもわたって{人々|ひとびと}の{信仰|しんこう}を{集|あつ}めてきた。
examples.english: This temple has an eternal history and has drawn the faith of people for many centuries.

notes:
Composed of {久|く} (long time) and {遠|おん} (distant). Originally a Buddhist term ({久遠|くおん}{実成|じつじょう} refers to the Buddha's eternal existence), it has expanded into literary and formal Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {久遠|くおん}の{時|とき} (eternal time)
- {久遠|くおん}の{平和|へいわ} (everlasting peace)
- {久遠|くおん}の{歴史|れきし} (eternal history)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {久遠|くおん}: eternity (literary, Buddhist origin)
- {永遠|えいえん}: eternity, forever (most common everyday word)
- {永久|えいきゅう}: permanence, perpetuity (formal, often in compounds)
